messages:
Anya Chen: Quick sync — finalizing launch criteria for the observability slice that bundles tracing hooks, cost breakdowns, and error analytics. Need final decisions on: default sampling, cost guardrails, acceptance metrics, and canary plan. Proposing default sampling 1% with automatic upsampling around error spikes, dashboard templates, and cost budgets with automatic alerts. @Sahil @Morgan please weigh in.

Sahil Patel: 1% default sounds OK for web traffic but what about low-volume customers? too noisy for them. Can we have tenant-level overrides + a per-route sample throttle?

Anya Chen: yes — tenant overrides are required. thinking of a sensible default UI in Console to flip sampling per-tenant + per-service. also need a fallback so we don't blow bill for trial accounts.

Morgan Lee: Agree on overrides. For rollout: canary with 5 customers (mix of high/low volume) for 2 weeks. Acceptance: <2% CPU increase on dataplane, cost delta <10% on sampled customers, and correct linking of spans -> traces in UI.

Jia Park: On sampling mechanics, suggest event-driven upsample rules: if error_rate(route) > 0.5% then temporarily increase sampling to 25% for that route for 5m. Also need a floor for sensitive routes (PII) — default to 0% unless allowed.

Anya Chen: love the error-driven boost. add a max per-tenant monthly token budget to avoid surprise bills. Product should show projected monthly cost when changing sampling.

Len Ortega: infra questions — we need two engineering tasks: (1) tracing hook config + UI + per-tenant override; (2) cost estimator that simulates token delta for different sampling profiles. ETA: 3 sprints for (1), 2 sprints for (2) if we can reuse existing billing calculator.

Sahil Patel: can we reduce effort by shipping a light rollout first: server-side sampling with CLI config, and Console only shows presets? Then iterate to full UI.

Anya Chen: yep, phased plan: Phase A = server-side config + dashboard templates + cost alerting; Phase B = Console tenant overrides + per-route UI + projected cost preview.

Jia Park: Sample config prototype (server-side) —
```json
{
 "sampling":{
  "default_rate":0.01,
  "error_rate_boost":0.25,
  "error_window_secs":300,
  "max_rate":1.0,
  "tenant_overrides":{
    "tenant_id":"<rate>"
  }
 }
}
```

Anya Chen: perfect. Add acceptance tests: synthetic trace generation to validate sampling & error upsampling logic. Also add a regression test that ensures sensitive routes remain at 0% unless explicitly marked.

Len Ortega: note for SRE: we need an alert when aggregated sampling tokens exceed expected budget for a customer — maybe integrate with existing cost-alert infra. @devops-bot can you create an alert template?

devops-bot: created alert template "observability-sampling-cost-exceed" with fields: customer_id, window=24h, threshold=monthly_budget_estimate*0.1. Link: https://infra.redwood/alerts/observability-sampling-cost-exceed

Morgan Lee: final questions for launch criteria checklist: (a) canary run for 2 weeks with 5 customers (ok), (b) dashboards: default trace view + top-error routes + cost-by-tenant widget (must ship Phase A), (c) regression tests run in CI and pass, (d) playbook: rollback if cost delta >20% or CPU increase >5% for hosts.

Anya Chen: I will assemble a concrete Launch Acceptance doc with those metrics and owners. Next steps: Len to create infra tasks and estimate, Jia to land server-side sampling prototype PR, Sahil to recruit canary customers, Morgan to make dashboard templates. I'll post the acceptance checklist in Confluence by EOD Friday.

Sahil Patel: ack, will ping a few customers. :thumbsup:

Jia Park: PR almost ready, will add tests today.

Len Ortega: creating tasks now, linking to sprint board.

devops-bot: reminder — scheduled canary window created for 2024-12-02 -> 2024-12-16
